
Concern:
Our children did not all experience their mTBIs at the same time point.
However, they are approximately equal in age.
It is not practical to for a dataset to have a tight control on both time since injury and age, particularly outside of the context of school-level athletics.
Our study assumes & tests the notion that there is heterogeneity at a persistent scale a


* The influence of nominal categorical variables such as sex or mechanism of injury on the results of the SNF subtyping is unclear
* Calculations for statistical power are unclear
* Similarly, clinically 'meaningful' effect sizes during statistical testing is unclear
* Current stage of proposed work does not validate the clinical utility of the subtyping
* Subjects that have sustained more than 1 mTBI (approximately 25% of the included subjects have sustained 2 mTBIs) are included, making it unclear if their impairments were the cause of the most recent mTBI or one of the earlier mTBIs
* The structure of the TBI-related data in the ABCD study is not compatible with typical criteria for diagnosing an mTBI [@WYA25C6X#Blennow_Etal_2016], making it possible for some subjects labeled as having had an mTBI to have actually had an injury that was more or less severe than a mild injury
* The structure of the TBI-related data also made it impossible to know if subjects had sustained more than one injury of the exact same type
* The control group proposed in objective 2-1 does not consist of orthopedic injury time-matched subjects
* Some variables used to define the subtypes were collected at chronic timepoints following the mTBI, which may reduce the relvance of these findings for subjects prior to an mTBI or in the acute stages following an mTBI
